[LERR.9.11] **Every fault names a rule.** The engine **must** give every
`TypeError`, `ComputationError` and `EngineError` a rule name, on the fault fact
where there is one ([LERR.9.2], [LERR.9.3]) and on the recorded atom and the
integrator callback always:

- a fault raised in an activation carries that activation's rule;
- a fault raised at a network node during matching, where no activation exists
  yet and the node may serve several rules, carries `$alpha_<id>` or
  `$beta_<id>`, from the kind and compiler-assigned id of the node that
  faulted;
- a fault with no node site at all carries `$engine`.

The name is a function of the artefact and the fault, so a replay reproduces it,
and the artefact maps the node id to a source line. The last two are synthetic
names ([LLEX.10.6.1]), so no author rule can bear
one. No fault carries an empty rule name.
